title: Stage 1: A model and a context
summary: Books in a SQLite database behind GET and POST endpoints, with a DbContext from dependency injection.

steps.title: The brief
body: A neighbourhood library wants an API for its front desk: books, authors, members and loans. You will build it over six stages, each tested by real HTTP requests against your running server, with the data in a real SQLite database.
- a `Book` entity and a `LibraryDb` context that receives its options through its constructor,
- `AddDbContext` with `Data Source=library.db`, and the database created at start-up,
- three endpoints: list books, get one, add one (with validation and a unique ISBN).
Each check starts your program in a fresh folder, so the database is always empty at first: the first book created gets id 1.

steps.prompt: Why does `LibraryDb` take `DbContextOptions<LibraryDb>` in its constructor instead of calling `UseSqlite` in `OnConfiguring`?
options: So the app (or a test) decides the provider and connection string, and DI can create the context per request
Because `OnConfiguring` does not work in ASP.NET Core
steps.explain: `AddDbContext` builds the options and passes them in. The same context class then works with SQLite in a test and SQL Server in production.

steps.prompt: Complete the registration and the start-up creation of the database.
steps.explain: The context is scoped, so outside a request you need your own scope to get one. `EnsureCreated` makes the tables (a real deployment would use migrations, module 6).

items: The title must not be blank
No two books share an ISBN
Every row has a primary key
steps.explain: Checking in the endpoint gives the client a clear error. A unique index makes the duplicate impossible even if two requests race past the check at the same moment.

steps.title: Books
prompt: Write the whole program. **Run checks** starts your server and calls it.
- `LibraryDb(DbContextOptions<LibraryDb> options)` with `DbSet<Book> Books`; register it with `AddDbContext` and `Data Source=library.db`; create the database at start-up.
- `GET /books`: every book, ordered by id, read without tracking.
- `POST /books` with a `record NewBook(string? Title, string? Isbn, int Year)`:
- `400` if the title is blank or the ISBN is not exactly 13 characters,
- `409 Conflict` if a book with that ISBN exists,
- otherwise trim the title, save, and answer `201` with a `Location` of `/books/{id}` and the book.
solution: await db.Books.FindAsync(id) is { } book ? Results.Ok(book) : Results.NotFound());
return Results.BadRequest(new { error = "a title and a 13-character isbn are required" });
return Results.Conflict(new { error = "a book with this isbn exists" });
var book = new Book { Title = input.Title.Trim(), Isbn = input.Isbn, Year = input.Year };
record NewBook(string? Title, string? Isbn, int Year);
template: public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
var dojoA = await Post(http, "/books", new { title = "  Dune ", isbn = "9780441013593", year = 1965 });
DojoWeb.Status("a second book: 201", 201, await Post(http, "/books", new { title = "Emma", isbn = "9780547773742", year = 1815 }));
DojoWeb.Status("a 10-character isbn: 400", 400, await Post(http, "/books", new { title = "X", isbn = "0441013597", year = 1 }));
DojoWeb.Status("no title: 400", 400, await Post(http, "/books", new { isbn = "9780061054884", year = 1 }));
DojoWeb.Status("a duplicate isbn: 409", 409, await Post(http, "/books", new { title = "Dune again", isbn = "9780441013593", year = 1 }));
Dojo.Eq("GET /books lists them by id", "Dune|Emma", Each(dojoList, "title"));
static async Task<HttpResponseMessage> Post(HttpClient http, string url, object body) => await http.PostAsJsonAsync(url, body);
static async Task<string?> Id(HttpResponseMessage r) => DojoWeb.Prop(await DojoWeb.Json(r), "id");
static string Each(JsonElement json, string prop) =>
json.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array ? string.Join("|", json.EnumerateArray().Select(x => DojoWeb.Prop(x, prop))) : "(not an array)";
static JsonElement Field(JsonElement json, string name)
foreach (var p in json.EnumerateObject()) if (string.Equals(p.Name, name, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)) return p.Value;
